n2ed07996f15.s: When Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956, its unicameral Legislative Assembly had how many members?
n2ed07996f15.x: In 1956 the AP Legislature was unicameral with an Assembly of 301 members; 175 is the present strength of residual AP.

na2411345a7d.s: How many seats in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly are reserved for SCs and STs respectively?
na2411345a7d.x: The AP Assembly has 29 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and 7 for Scheduled Tribes.

n4142145e3ba.s: How many seats did the YSRCP win in the 16th AP Legislative Assembly (2024), leaving it without official Opposition status?
n4142145e3ba.x: The YSRCP won 11 of the 175 seats, below the one-tenth needed for official Opposition status.

ne0e8a491185.s: Under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the proposed Assembly strength for Andhra Pradesh is:
ne0e8a491185.x: Section 26 contemplates 225 seats for AP and 153 for Telangana, subject to Article 170; the increase is not yet implemented.

n879c0948325.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Committee on Public Undertakings exists:
o: in place of the Estimates Committee
in place of the Public Accounts Committee
in place of both the Estimates Committee and the PAC
in addition to the Estimates Committee and the PAC
n879c0948325.x: AP has the Committee on Public Undertakings in addition to, not instead of, the Estimates and Public Accounts Committees.

n2cff86e86f6.s: Under Article 128, the CJI may request a retired judge to sit in the Supreme Court with the previous consent of the:
n2cff86e86f6.x: Article 128 needs the President's previous consent and the retired judge's consent; such a judge has full powers but is not deemed a regular judge.

n547b98e227e.s: A Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of ____ and resigns by writing to the ____.
n547b98e227e.x: A Supreme Court judge retires at 65 and addresses his resignation to the President; 62 is the High Court retirement age.

nf98fe3b488a.s: The Law Commission's 214th Report on judicial appointments was submitted in:
nf98fe3b488a.x: The 214th Report was submitted in 2008, not 1998; the 14th Report came in 1958.

nindian-polity-69-48.s: A Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court under Article 145(3) consists of a minimum of:
nindian-polity-69-48.x: Under Article 145(3), at least five judges hear cases on interpretation of the Constitution and references under Article 143.

nindian-polity-47-10.s: Which Judges Case held that 'consultation' means 'concurrence' and gave birth to the Collegium?
nindian-polity-47-10.x: The Second Judges Case (1993) reversed the 1981 ruling, held that consultation means concurrence and created the collegium.

nindian-polity-47-11.s: The NJAC was struck down in 2015 because executive involvement in it was held to infringe:
o: judicial independence, part of the Basic Structure
nindian-polity-47-11.x: The Court held that the executive's role in the NJAC threatened judicial independence, which is part of the Basic Structure.

n2a46ad3d7ba.s: Civil and criminal contempt are defined by:
n2a46ad3d7ba.x: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 defines civil and criminal contempt; the Constitution confers contempt powers but does not define contempt.

nebb79a568c2.s: Which Article gives the Supreme Court of India the advisory jurisdiction that the US Supreme Court lacks?
nebb79a568c2.x: India's Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143; the US Supreme Court has none.

nindian-polity-30-8.s: On a reference under Article 143(2) on a pre-Constitution treaty or agreement, the Supreme Court:
o: may refuse to give its opinion
gives an opinion binding on the President
can advise only on questions of fact
nindian-polity-30-8.x: Under Article 143(2) the Court must give its opinion; its advice does not bind the President.

nindian-polity-69-15.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 143?
o: The opinion of the Supreme Court is binding on the President
Under Article 143(1), the President may refer questions of law or fact of public importance
Under Article 143(1), the Supreme Court may tender its opinion
Under Article 143(2), the Supreme Court must tender its opinion on pre-Constitution matters
nindian-polity-69-15.x: The advisory opinion under Article 143 does not bind the President; the other three statements are correct.

nindian-polity-69-7.s: Which of the following falls within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 131?
o: Recovery of damages by a private party against the Union
A legal-right dispute between one State and another
nindian-polity-69-7.x: Article 131 covers legal-right disputes between the Centre and States or between States; private damages suits, water disputes and Finance Commission matters are excluded.

nindian-polity-69-35.s: Inter-State water disputes are kept out of the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction by Article:
nindian-polity-69-35.x: Inter-State water disputes fall under Article 262 and are excluded from Article 131; Article 280 relates to Finance Commission matters.

n989c0a29fc2.s: Which Article applies the Supreme Court's removal provisions to High Court judges?
n989c0a29fc2.x: Article 124(4) deals with removal of a Supreme Court judge and Article 218 applies it to High Court judges.

nace01ee4d3f.s: How many Supreme Court judges have so far been removed through the constitutional removal process?
nace01ee4d3f.x: No judge has been removed so far: the motion against V. Ramaswami failed and Soumitra Sen resigned before the Lok Sabha vote.

n33e5221e224.s: A motion for the removal of a judge must be signed by at least how many Lok Sabha members?
n33e5221e224.x: The motion needs 100 Lok Sabha members or 50 Rajya Sabha members.

nindian-polity-30-9.s: The address for removal of a Supreme Court judge must be passed in each House of Parliament by:
o: a majority of total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting
two-thirds of the total membership alone
three-fourths of those present and voting
nindian-polity-30-9.x: Removal needs a special majority in each House: a majority of total membership plus two-thirds present and voting.

n9d86f183399.s: Which of the following Chief Justices of India was from Andhra Pradesh?
n9d86f183399.x: K. Subba Rao and N.V. Ramana were the Chief Justices of India from Andhra Pradesh.

nindian-polity-70-12.s: To be appointed a High Court judge, a citizen must have held judicial office or practised as a High Court advocate for at least:
nindian-polity-70-12.x: Ten years in judicial office or as a High Court advocate qualifies; the distinguished-jurist route exists only for the Supreme Court.

nindian-polity-71-24.s: Which route to appointment is available for a Supreme Court judge but not for a High Court judge?
o: Ten years as a High Court advocate
Ten years in a judicial office
nindian-polity-71-24.x: Under Article 124(3)(c) a distinguished jurist can be made a Supreme Court judge; no such route exists for High Courts.

nindian-polity-71-6.s: A High Court judge takes his oath of office before the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
nindian-polity-71-6.x: The oath is taken before the Governor (Article 219), though the resignation is addressed to the President.

nindian-polity-71-8.s: Which Article deals with the transfer of a High Court judge?
nindian-polity-71-8.x: Transfer is under Article 222; Article 219 is the oath, 215 the High Court as Court of Record and 129 the Supreme Court as Court of Record.

nindian-polity-71-14.s: The appointment of an Acting Judge of a High Court ends when he attains the age of:
nindian-polity-71-14.x: Acting judges fill in for absent permanent judges or those acting as Chief Justice, and their appointment ends at 62.

nindian-polity-71-16.s: The salary and allowances of a High Court judge are charged on the:
nindian-polity-71-16.x: A High Court judge's salary is charged on the State's Consolidated Fund, while the pension is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

nindian-polity-71-22.s: The retirement age of High Court judges was raised from 60 to 62 by the:
nindian-polity-71-22.x: The 15th Amendment (1963) raised the High Court retirement age from 60 to 62.

n4f748bf4936.s: Article 214 of the Constitution provides for:
o: a common High Court for two or more States
appointment of High Court judges by the President
extension of High Court jurisdiction to a Union Territory
a High Court for each State
n4f748bf4936.x: Article 214 provides a High Court for each State; a common High Court is under Article 231 and UT jurisdiction under Article 230.

nindian-polity-70-10.s: Restriction on practice after being a permanent High Court judge is dealt with in Article:
nindian-polity-70-10.x: Article 220 restricts practice after retirement; 223 is the acting Chief Justice, 226 writs and 227 superintendence.

nindian-polity-70-19.s: Which High Court has jurisdiction over Lakshadweep?
nindian-polity-70-19.x: The Kerala High Court covers Lakshadweep, while the Madras High Court covers Puducherry.

nindian-polity-51-4.s: The High Courts share judicial review with the Supreme Court through their writ jurisdiction under Article:
nindian-polity-51-4.x: The Supreme Court holds writ power under Article 32 and the High Courts under Article 226, so judicial review is shared.

nindian-polity-71-10.s: A retired Supreme Court judge may plead:
o: in no court or before any authority in India
in any court except the Supreme Court
nindian-polity-71-10.x: A retired Supreme Court judge cannot plead anywhere in India; a retired High Court judge may plead in the Supreme Court and other High Courts.

nindian-polity-71-30.s: An Additional Judge of a High Court may be appointed for a period not exceeding:
nindian-polity-71-30.x: Additional judges are appointed for a temporary rise in work or arrears for at most two years and cannot serve past 62.

nindian-polity-30-22.s: As a Court of Record, the Supreme Court's judgments:
o: can be questioned in any subordinate court
have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned in a subordinate court
nindian-polity-30-22.x: Judgments of a Court of Record serve as evidence and cannot be questioned when produced before a lower court.

nindian-polity-70-48.s: Article 215 of the Constitution makes which of the following a Court of Record?
nindian-polity-70-48.x: Article 215 makes the High Courts Courts of Record; the Supreme Court's provision is Article 129.

nindian-polity-71-36.s: Administrative decisions of a High Court Chief Justice, such as staff appointments, can be challenged by writ under Article:
nindian-polity-71-36.x: Administrative actions of a High Court Chief Justice are open to writs under Article 226, so there is no absolute immunity.

nindian-polity-51-7.s: Which Article is the primary textual foundation for striking down laws that abridge Fundamental Rights?
nindian-polity-51-7.x: Article 13(2) makes laws abridging Fundamental Rights void; review of the Court's own judgments is Article 137 and complete justice is Article 142.

nindian-polity-1-8.s: The presidential form of government was first formed in:
nindian-polity-1-8.x: The presidential form began in the USA, while the parliamentary form began in Great Britain.

nindian-polity-1-14.s: The Basic Structure doctrine was first propounded in which case?
nindian-polity-1-14.x: The Basic Structure doctrine was first propounded in Kesavananda Bharati in 1973.

n6712fe4d6f6.s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided the common High Court for Telangana and Andhra Pradesh?
n6712fe4d6f6.x: Section 30 provided the common High Court at Hyderabad; Section 31 the separate AP High Court and Section 32 its judges.

new.s: Before 1956, the Andhra State Legislative Assembly met at:
new.x: The Andhra State Assembly met at Kurnool before 1956; from 1956 the seat was Hyderabad.

new.s: Since 2017, the AP Legislature has met in an interim building at:
new.x: Since 2017 the Legislature has met at Amaravati in an interim building at Velagapudi.

new.s: The first meeting of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly was held on:
new.x: The AP Legislative Assembly first met on 3 December 1956.

new.s: In which year did the AP Legislature become bicameral with the creation of the Legislative Council?
new.x: The Council was created in 1958; it was abolished in 1985 and revived in 2007.

new.s: Who was the first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly (1956)?
new.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker; Kalluri Subbarao was the first Deputy Speaker.

new.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council?
new.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao was the first Council Chairman; Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker of the Assembly.

new.s: Who was the first Speaker of the residual Andhra Pradesh Assembly (2014-19)?
new.x: Kodela Siva Prasada Rao was the first Speaker of residual AP; Ayyanna Patrudu is Speaker in 2026.

new.s: Which AP Legislative Assembly had the most independents ever, 68 of 294 members?
new.x: The 4th Assembly (1967) had the most independents ever, 68 of 294 members.

new.s: B.V. Subba Reddy, who left the Congress in 1955 and won as an independent, became Speaker from:
new.x: B.V. Subba Reddy won as an independent and was later Speaker from 1962.

new.s: The 16th Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly was constituted in:
new.x: Residual AP continued the numbering: 14th (2014), 15th (2019) and 16th (2024).

new.s: In the 16th AP Legislative Assembly (2024), the NDA won how many of the 175 seats?
new.x: The NDA won 164 of 175 seats: TDP 135, JSP 21 and BJP 8.

new.s: The January 2020 resolution of the AP Assembly to abolish the Legislative Council was:
o: struck down by the High Court
new.x: The abolition resolution of January 2020 was withdrawn in November 2021, and the Council continues.

new.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the AP Legislative Council is wrongly matched?
new.x: The Council was revived in 2007 under the AP Legislative Council Act, 2005; 2005 is the year of the Act, not the revival.

new.s: Existing MLCs were allotted between AP and Telangana under Section 22(2) of the AP Reorganisation Act through the:
new.x: Section 22(2) allotted existing MLCs between the two States under the Fourth Schedule.

new.s: In the 58-member AP Legislative Council, how many members are elected by graduates?
new.x: Graduates elect 5 members (1/12); local authorities and MLAs elect 20 each and the Governor nominates 8.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 58-member AP Legislative Council:
1. Local authorities elect 20 members.
2. MLAs elect 20 members.
3. Teachers elect 8 members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Local authorities and MLAs elect 20 each; teachers elect 5, while 8 are nominated by the Governor.

new.s: Under Section 20 of the AP Reorganisation Act, the five-year term of the Assembly is under Article:
new.x: Section 20 provides the five-year term under Article 172(1).

new.s: Under the 2008 delimitation, how many Assembly constituencies does Visakhapatnam district have?
new.x: Visakhapatnam has 15 seats (not 14); East Godavari has the most with 19.

new.s: The chairpersons of the committees of the AP Legislature are named by the:
new.x: Committee members are elected from the House and their chairpersons are named by the Speaker, not the Governor.

new.s: By convention, the chair of the Public Accounts Committee of the AP Legislature goes to the:
new.x: By convention the PAC chair goes to the Opposition.

new.s: The Federal Court, which the Supreme Court replaced in 1950, was set up in:
new.x: The Federal Court was set up in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935.

new.s: Appeals to the Privy Council from India were abolished in:
new.x: Privy Council appeals were abolished in 1949; the Supreme Court replaced the Federal Court on 26 January 1950.

new.s: As of May 2026, the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court including the Chief Justice of India is:
new.x: The 2026 Ordinance raised the strength to 38 (CJI + 37); 34 was the 2019 figure.

new.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 was promulgated under Article:
new.x: The Ordinance was issued under Article 123 and notified on 16 May 2026.

new.s: The convention of appointing the senior-most judge as CJI was broken in 1973 by the appointment of:
new.x: A.N. Ray's appointment in 1973 broke the seniority convention; M.H. Beg's followed in 1977.

new.s: The age of a Supreme Court judge is determined as Parliament provides by law under Article:
new.x: Article 124(2A), inserted by the 15th Amendment (1963), lets Parliament provide for determining a judge's age.

new.s: The form of oath of a Supreme Court judge is set out in the:
new.x: The oath is taken before the President in the form given in the Third Schedule; the Second Schedule deals with salaries.

new.s: Which Article provides for the appointment of an acting Chief Justice of India?
new.x: Article 126 provides for an acting CJI appointed by the President; 127 covers ad hoc and 128 retired judges.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court:
1. Additional judges may be appointed to it.
2. An ad hoc judge is appointed by the CJI with the President's previous consent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: There are no additional judges in the Supreme Court; they exist only in High Courts. Ad hoc judges are appointed by the CJI with the President's previous consent.

new.s: The Third Judges Case (1998) arose from a:
new.x: The Third Judges Case was a Presidential Reference under Article 143(1); it enlarged the collegium to CJI + 4.

new.s: How many States ratified the 99th Constitutional Amendment on the NJAC?
new.x: The 99th Amendment was ratified by 16 States before receiving assent on 31 December 2014.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the National Judicial Appointments Commission?
new.x: The NJAC had the CJI, two senior-most SC judges, the Law Minister and two eminent persons; the Attorney-General was not a member.

new.s: The Fourth Judges Case bench that struck down the NJAC was led by:
new.x: The five-judge bench was led by J.S. Khehar; J. Chelameswar was the lone dissent.

new.s: The NJAC was struck down by a majority of:
new.x: The five-judge bench struck down the NJAC 4:1, with J. Chelameswar dissenting.

new.s: Special leave to appeal under Article 136 cannot be granted against a judgment of:
o: a court or tribunal under the Armed Forces law
new.x: Under Article 136(2), special leave lies against any court or tribunal except a military one.

new.s: Election disputes relating to Parliament and State Legislatures are decided by the:
new.x: Election disputes of Parliament and Legislatures are outside Article 131 and go to the High Courts.

new.s: An appeal under Article 132 in a case of constitutional interpretation requires a certificate under Article:
new.x: Article 132 appeals need a High Court certificate under Article 134A; an SLP under Article 136 needs none.

new.s: The 16th Presidential Reference to the Supreme Court (November 2025) concerned:
o: delay in the Gujarat Assembly elections
new.x: The 16th Presidential Reference (Nov 2025) concerned timelines for Bills; the Gujarat election reference was made in 2002.

new.s: The curative petition was evolved by the Supreme Court in:
o: Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra (2002)
Anil Kumar Jain v. Maya Jain
new.x: The curative petition comes from Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra (2002) and lies after a review is dismissed.

new.s: Under Article 141, the law declared by the Supreme Court:
o: is binding only on the High Courts
new.x: Article 141 makes the law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all courts.

new.s: Under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, the committee that inquires into charges against a judge has:
new.x: A three-member committee is formed: an SC judge or the CJI, an HC Chief Justice and a distinguished jurist.

new.s: Which Article bars a State Legislature from discussing the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge?
new.x: Article 211 bars State Legislatures and Article 121 bars Parliament, except on a removal motion.

new.s: A High Court is a Court of Record under Article:
new.x: Article 215 makes a High Court a Court of Record; Article 129 does so for the Supreme Court.

new.s: Unlike the Supreme Court, whose strength is fixed by Parliament, the strength of a High Court is fixed by the:
new.x: Under Article 216 the President fixes the strength of a High Court; Parliament fixes the Supreme Court's.

new.s: Who succeeded H.J. Kania as Chief Justice of India?
new.x: H.J. Kania was the first CJI, followed by M. Patanjali Sastri.

new.s: Justice M. Fathima Beevi later became the first Muslim woman Governor of:
new.x: Fathima Beevi, the first woman SC judge (1989), later became Governor of Tamil Nadu and the first woman NHRC member.

new.s: Article 230, on extending or excluding High Court jurisdiction over a Union Territory, was inserted by the:
new.x: Article 230 came with the 7th Amendment, 1956; the 15th Amendment inserted Article 224A.

new.s: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands fall under the jurisdiction of which High Court?
new.x: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are under the Calcutta High Court, with a circuit bench at Port Blair.

new.s: Which three High Courts were created in January 2013?
new.x: Meghalaya, Manipur and Tripura got High Courts in January 2013, working from 23 March 2013.

new.s: The oldest High Court in India is the:
new.x: The Calcutta High Court (2 July 1862) is the oldest; Bombay and Madras followed in 1862.

new.s: With the separate Andhra Pradesh High Court on 1 January 2019, the number of High Courts in India became:
new.x: The AP High Court became the 25th High Court, taking the count from 24 to 25.

new.s: The 114th Constitutional Amendment Bill (2010) sought to raise the retirement age of High Court judges to:
new.x: The 114th Amendment Bill (2010) sought 65; the retirement age remains 62.

new.s: Justice Yashwant Varma, whose inquiry report was to be tabled despite his resignation, was formerly a judge of which High Court?
new.x: Yashwant Varma was formerly of the Allahabad High Court, not Madras; G.R. Swaminathan is the Madras HC judge.

new.s: Article 222 provides for the transfer of:
o: both Supreme Court and High Court judges
new.x: Article 222 lets the President transfer High Court judges after consulting the CJI; there is no provision to transfer SC judges.

new.s: As of 18 September 2025, the sanctioned strength of all High Courts together was:
new.x: The sanctioned strength was 1,122, of which 804 posts were filled.

new.s: Under Article 227(4), a High Court's superintendence does not extend to:
new.x: Article 227 covers all subordinate courts and tribunals except those under the Armed Forces (227(4)).

new.s: The first major law on contempt of court in India was the:
new.x: The Contempt of Court Act, 1926 was the first major law; the 1971 Act followed the H.N. Sanyal Committee.

new.s: Under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, scandalising the court or obstructing justice is:
new.x: Criminal contempt covers scandalising or obstructing justice; civil contempt is wilful disobedience of a court order.

new.s: The first Chief Justice of the Andhra State High Court at Guntur (1954) was:
new.x: The Andhra State High Court opened at Guntur on 5 July 1954 with Koka Subba Rao as first Chief Justice.

new.s: Who was the first regular Chief Justice of the separate Andhra Pradesh High Court (October 2019)?
new.x: J.K. Maheshwari was the first regular CJ; C. Praveen Kumar was the first acting CJ from 1 January 2019.

new.s: Who was recommended in February 2026 as the first woman Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court?
new.x: Lisa Gill was recommended in February 2026 as the first woman Chief Justice of the AP High Court.

new.s: The Andhra State High Court moved to Hyderabad as the High Court of united Andhra Pradesh on:
new.x: The High Court moved from Guntur to Hyderabad on 1 November 1956.

new.s: For direct appointment as a District Judge under Article 233, an advocate needs at least how many years of practice?
new.x: Article 233 requires 7 years as an advocate; a High Court judge needs 10 years.

new.s: Under Article 234, the Governor makes rules for recruiting judicial officers other than district judges after consulting the High Court and the:
new.x: Article 234 requires consultation with the State Public Service Commission and the High Court.

new.s: The All India Judicial Service is enabled by which Article, though it is not yet created?
new.x: Article 312, as amended by the 42nd Amendment, enables the AIJS, but it has not been created.

new.s: Lok Adalats have their statutory basis in the:
new.x: Lok Adalats work under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987; Gram Nyayalayas under the 2008 Act.

new.s: An award of a Lok Adalat is:
o: deemed a civil court decree, final with no appeal
new.x: A Lok Adalat award is deemed a decree of a civil court and is final, with no appeal.

new.s: The presiding officer of a Gram Nyayalaya is called a:
new.x: A Gram Nyayalaya is presided over by a Nyayadhikari of Judicial Magistrate First Class rank.

new.s: Gram Nyayalayas are set up at the level of the:
new.x: Gram Nyayalayas are mobile courts at the intermediate panchayat level under the Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008.

new.s: Marbury v. Madison (1803), the origin of judicial review, was decided under US Chief Justice:
new.x: Marbury v. Madison (1803) was decided under Chief Justice John Marshall; its roots go back to Sir Edward Coke.

new.s: Which Article bars courts from inquiring into the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor?
new.x: Article 163(3) bars inquiry into advice to the Governor; Article 74(2) does so for the President.

new.s: Which case held that Article 361 protects only the office-holder and that decisions remain reviewable on mala fides?
new.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) held that decisions of the President or Governor are reviewable on mala fides or irrelevant grounds.

new.s: Clause (4) of Article 329A, inserted by the 39th Amendment to shield the PM's election, was struck down in:
new.x: Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) struck down clause (4) of Article 329A as violating the basic structure.

new.s: The 38th Amendment's bar on reviewing the President's satisfaction under Articles 123, 213 and 352 was reversed by the:
new.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) reversed the 38th; the 43rd restored HC review of central laws barred by the 42nd.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutionally permissible way to overcome a judicial judgment?
o: A validating law removing the basis of the judgment
A constitutional amendment subject to the Basic Structure
A legislative resolution simply overruling the judgment
new.x: The legislature cannot simply overrule a judgment; it may remove its basis by law, amend the Constitution or seek review.

new.s: Which case is associated with police reforms?
new.x: Prakash Singh is the police reforms case; Olga Tellis concerned livelihood and Vishaka workplace harassment.

new.s: Which 2007 case held that judges must not encroach on the legislature or executive, an instance of judicial restraint?
o: Divisional Manager, Aravali Golf Club v. Chander Hass
new.x: Aravali Golf Club v. Chander Hass (2007) is a restraint ruling; the others are activism cases.

new.s: State of Rajasthan v. Union of India (1977), where the Court declined a political question, is an example of:
new.x: By declining a political question, the Court in State of Rajasthan (1977) showed judicial restraint.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about judicial review and judicial activism:
1. Judicial review asks 'Is the law valid?'
2. Judicial activism asks 'Is the law just?'
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Review is interpretative and asks whether the law is valid; activism is creative and asks whether it is just.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Section 17 allots 175 Assembly seats to AP and 119 to Telangana
Section 21 sends the Deputy Speaker to Telangana
Section 25 sends the Deputy Chairman of the Council to Telangana
Section 21 sends the Speaker to Telangana
new.x: Under Section 21 the AP Speaker continues and the Deputy Speaker goes to Telangana.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about judges under Articles 126-128?
o: Article 126 – acting CJI appointed by the President
Article 127 – ad hoc judge appointed by the CJI with the President's previous consent
Article 128 – retired judge sits with the President's and the judge's consent
Article 127 – ad hoc judge appointed by the President on the collegium's advice
new.x: An ad hoc judge is appointed by the CJI with the President's previous consent, not by the President on collegium advice.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 234 – Recruitment of other judicial officers
Article 235 – High Court control over subordinate courts
new.x: The definition of 'district judge' is in Article 236; Article 237 lets the Governor extend the provisions to magistrates.
